item.title: Hawaiian homes devastated by Hurricane Lowell
item.description: Hurricane Lowell lashed the Hawaiian islands with up to 2 feet of rain in some parts, 90-mph winds and monster waves. Carter Evans reports and Rob Marciano hs the forecast.

item.title: Lindsay Clancy's lawyer asks Trump to pardon her, despite it being a state case
item.description: Lindsay Clancy's lawyer spoke with CBS News Boston on Tuesday, explaining why he'd asked President Trump to somehow pardon her, as she is still under state indictment for killing her three children. Shanelle Kaul reports.

item.title: Lindsay Clancy juror speaks after mistrial: "There was so much doubt"
item.description: A woman who served as a juror in Lindsay Clancy's high-profile Massachusetts murder trial provided a look at deliberations, saying there was too much doubt for her to reach a guilty verdict.

item.title: Barack Obama on the operation to find, kill Osama bin Laden | 60 Minutes Archive
item.description: In 2011, then-President Barack Obama sat down with 60 Minutes for his first interview after the killing of Osama bin Laden. He described what went through his mind as he watched the operation unfold.

item.title: Trump administration to ban some Canadian motorcycles, dairy, alcohol
item.description: The Trump administration moved Tuesday to ban imports of Canadian motorcycles, some dairy products and most types of alcohol starting later this month, intensifying the trade war between the two countries.

item.title: New Hampshire Senate race set between Pappas and Sununu after projected primary wins
item.description: Rep. Chris Pappas defeated democratic socialist Karishma Manzur in the Democratic primary, while former Sen. John Sununu defeated Scott Brown in the GOP contest.

item.title: Federal judge backs Missouri's new House map after Supreme Court rebuffs case
item.description: A federal judge ruled that Missouri should use a new congressional map that favors Republicans for now, hours after the U.S. Supreme Court left in place a ruling from the state's highest court directing Missouri to use an older map.

item.title: Supreme Court rebuffs Missouri's request for new House map favoring Republicans
item.description: The Supreme Court on Tuesday denied an emergency application to block a Missouri Supreme Court ruling barring the state from using its new congressional map, which favors Republicans. CBS News White House reporter Aaron Navarro has more.

item.title: Lowell lashes Hawaii, knocking out power to thousands as flood risk continues
item.description: Fierce winds downed trees and caused widespread power outages on the island of Kauai, home to 73,000 residents.

item.title: 2 paintings by Renoir stolen from museum in France, officials say
item.description: Authorities are seeking thieves who broke into the Renoir Museum in the French Riviera and stole two paintings by the impressionist master, local authorities say.

item.title: Hurricane Marie damages several Southern California homes
item.description: Hurricane Marie damaged several homes across Southern California. CBS News Los Angeles' Jeff Nguyen is in Malibu with a look at the aftermath.

item.title: Renoir paintings worth millions stolen from French museum, thieves on the run
item.description: Four Renoir paintings worth an estimated $10.5 million were stolen from a French museum, though they abandoned two of the paintings as they fled. Two suspected thieves are still on the run.

item.title: 16 years after winning "Australia's Got Talent," dad becomes musical sensation for babies
item.description: The comeback career of Lenny Pearce is pretty much a dream come true for musicians. His boy band won "Australia's Got Talent" in 2010, but after a while, the attention faded. Now, he's become a worldwide hit for babies and toddlers who play remixed nursery rhymes at home. Tony Dokoupil has the story.

item.title: U.S. consumers to face higher prices on milk, cheese amid Canada's retaliatory tariffs
item.description: U.S. consumers can expect to see higher prices on some dairy products in the wake of Canada's retaliatory tariffs amid President Trump's trade war. Rick Naerebout, CEO of the Idaho Dairymen's Association and the Washington State Dairy Federation, joins "The Daily Report."

item.title: 9/11 victim's son honors father through work at Tunnel to Towers Foundation
item.description: Stephen Siller Jr., whose New York City firefighter father died on 9/11, has spent the last four months displaying a massive steel beam from the World Trade Center's south tower across the country as a symbol of what was lost in the attacks. CBS News chief Washington correspondent Major Garrett spoke with Siller about the "Steel Across America" campaign.

item.title: U.S. forces hit Iran-linked oil tankers as oil nears $100 a barrel
item.description: Oil prices are rising steadily with no end in sight to the U.S.-Iran standoff impeding tanker traffic in the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: Drug drone activity at U.S.-Mexico border drops 75% after U.S. uses laser weapon, military says
item.description: The use of drones connected to drug trafficking has sharply declined at the U.S.-Mexico border after the U.S began using a laser weapon to target the devices, according to U.S. military officials. CBS News' Eleanor Watson has more.

item.title: U.S. forces destroy 5 Iranian oil tankers, CENTCOM says
item.description: U.S. Central Command announced Tuesday that American forces destroyed five Iranian oil tankers after Tehran targeted a U.S. Navy warship with ballistic missiles. CBS News Pentagon reporter Eleanor Watson has the latest.

item.title: Canada's retaliatory tariffs on $20 billion in U.S. goods take effect
item.description: Canada's steep retaliatory tariffs on $20 billion in U.S. goods took effect just after midnight ET on Tuesday, deepening the trade war between the two countries.

item.title: Canada imposes tariffs on U.S. dairy, steel, aluminum and appliances
item.description: Canadian tariffs took effect on about $20 billion worth of U.S. goods on Tuesday. It marked the latest escalation in a trade war with no clear end in sight. Nancy Cordes has more details.

item.title: 4 found dead after Miami family's small plane goes missing off Bahamas
item.description: A small plane carrying four family members flying back home to Florida went missing off the Bahamas, the U.S. Coast Guard and authorities in the Bahamas said.

item.title: 9/11 responder recounts rescue and recovery efforts, health struggles after attacks
item.description: Richard Palmer, a retired warden at the New York City Corrections Department who assisted with evacuation efforts on 9/11, joins "The Daily Report" to tell his story as NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani says residents were misled about air quality in the aftermath of the attacks.

item.title: Victims identified in deadly plane crash at Miami International Airport
item.description: The Amazon cargo plane crashed off the end of a runway at Miami International Airport on Sunday, leaving five people dead and five others injured.

item.title: Bodies of Miami family found after plane went missing off the Bahamas, authorities say
item.description: Four bodies were found after a small plane went missing near the Bahamas. Skyler Henry reports on this and the deadly Amazon cargo jet crash.

item.title: Texas Tribune Festival to feature Marjorie Taylor Greene, James Talarico and more
item.description: The Texas Tribune Festival, in its 16th year, will take place in Austin in late September. High-profile speakers include Texas Democratic Senate candidate James Talarico, former Republican Rep. Marjorie Taylor Greene of Georgia and more. Texas Tribune CEO Sarah Adler Hartman joins CBS News to discuss.

item.title: Former senators face off in New Hampshire GOP primary
item.description: New Hampshire primary voters are at the polls on Tuesday, as Democrats and Republicans select their nominees for the Senate. The Republican primary features two former senators: John Sununu of New Hampshire and Scott Brown, who used to represent Massachusetts. Political strategists Adam Green and Tim Chapman join with analysis.

item.title: What Canada's retaliatory tariffs could mean for U.S. consumers as Trump threatens escalation
item.description: Canada is imposing retaliatory tariffs on $20 billion in American goods as President Trump threatens further escalation, including a ban on the Canadian plane manufacturer Bombardier. CBS News' Olivia Rinaldi has more.

item.title: TSA program will allow some people to go through security without a ticket
item.description: The Transportation Security Administration has launched a new program at 13 airports, allowing eligible TSA PreCheck members without plane tickets to pass through security and enter the gates.

item.title: 9/8: The Takeout with Major Garrett
item.description: Retaliatory Canadian tariffs on U.S. goods take effect; Republicans gather in Dallas for midterm convention.

item.title: Goldman Sachs warns oil prices could hit $120 as U.S. fuel costs surge
item.description: Higher gas and diesel prices have cost Americans an additional $100 billion since the Iran war began, according to a Brown University tracker.
